transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-30
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood Solutions), Rajiv Menon (CTO, NimbleGrid), Sara Lopez (Lead ML Eng), Tom Brooks (Platform Eng), Priya Shah (Security)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough): Discussed integration options, required connectors for LangChain/LlamaIndex and gateway patterns; customer wants perf baseline and security docs.

00:00 - Alex Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, do we have all the right people?
00:05 - Rajiv Menon: Yep, this is Rajiv. Sara and Tom are on. Priya just joined.
00:12 - Maya Patel: Awesome. Quick agenda: we want to cover SDKs, langchain/llama index support, gateway/proxy patterns, rate limits, and observability hooks. Leave time at the end for next steps. Sound good?
00:20 - Rajiv Menon: Sounds good. Our main concern is throughput and predictable costs — and security. We'll probably lean toward Dedicated if the numbers work.

01:05 - Sara Lopez: Quick background: we run real-time personalization pipelines, about 6k reqs/sec peak, but many are short prompts. We use a proxy in front of third-party LLMs today to centralize auth and caching.
01:20 - Tom Brooks: our infra is k8s on GCP, we have a gateway service that does tracing and token accounting. We need to see how Redwood fits into that model.

02:10 - Maya Patel: Got it. On the SDK side, Redwood has Python and JS SDKs; we also have official connectors/recipes for LangChain and LlamaIndex. The LangChain stuff is updated for the new chains interface, and we include examples for streaming and function call patterns.
02:30 - Sara Lopez: Are those SDKs open source? We prefer to vet code.
02:35 - Alex Chen: Yes — SDKs and examples are in our public GitHub. We'll share links after this call. The LangChain connector is small — mainly a few adaptors. There's also a LlamaIndex connector for retrieval-augmented generation.

04:00 - Rajiv Menon: On the gateway: our gateway adds JWT auth, per-tenant quotas, and does prefix caching for common prompts. Can Redwood integrate with a proxy model where the gateway injects keys and routes to either Hosted or Dedicated endpoints?
04:18 - Maya Patel: Absolutely. We support API keys per-tenant, and our endpoints accept forwarded auth headers. Typical pattern: gateway authenticates, then signs requests with a service key to Redwood. For Dedicated, we can expose a private ingress IP or a VPC peering connection so your gateway talks directly to the dedicated pool.
04:45 - Tom Brooks: If we use that pattern, how do we do per-tenant quotas? We currently enforce quotas in the gateway by counting tokens. Is there token usage headers or a way to get token counts back?
05:05 - Jordan Li: We emit token usage in responses and via our usage API. There's a token-level cost field in the response metadata and real-time metrics in the Console. You can also stream usage logs to your observability stack (we support Datadog, New Relic, and exportable Prometheus metrics).

06:10 - Priya Shah: For security, we need to know about encryption at rest, KMS support, audit logs, and SSO. Also whether customer data ever hits a shared filesystem.
06:28 - Alex Chen: We have SOC2 compliance; Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and optional key management integration (KMS/HSM). We provide audit logs and a private control plane option for Private deployments. We'll share the compliance pack.

08:00 - Sara Lopez: For LangChain, how easy is it to swap Redwood as a provider? Are there any behavioral differences (streaming, partial tokens) we should be aware of?
08:20 - Maya Patel: The LangChain adapter implements streaming and supports partial tokens. There are slight differences in stop sequences and function calling semantics compared to some other providers — the adapter normalizes that. We'll include code snippets showing streaming iterators and recomposition.

10:30 - Rajiv Menon: On rate limits, our traffic is spiky — 6k RPS at peaks for short bursts. We want predictable throttling and graceful degradation. How do rate limits and quotas work across Hosted vs Dedicated?
10:50 - Maya Patel: Hosted has global rate limits to protect shared infrastructure; they are higher for paid plans. Dedicated has configurable per-pool concurrency and throughput settings. You can set soft and hard quotas; soft quotas trigger throttling with 429s and an optional retry-after header, and we support token-based quotas too. For spikes we recommend burst capacity configuration or autoscale policies.

12:00 - Tom Brooks: Does Redwood provide client-side retry guidance? We currently implement exponential backoff with jitter.
12:08 - Jordan Li: Yes — our SDKs include retry middleware with configurable backoff and idempotency helpers. For streaming and function calls you can customize behavior. We'll share recommended retry settings for Dedicated vs Hosted.

14:20 - Sara Lopez: Observability — we need traces that tie a user request through our gateway into Redwood to see per-request latency and token cost. Is there a way to inject our trace IDs and have Redwood propagate them into logs/traces?
14:40 - Maya Patel: We support passing traceparent/trace headers and will stitch those into our traces. In the Console you can filter by trace id and get token-level breakdowns. We also provide trace export to your OTLP collector and logs via structured JSON to your logging sink.

16:00 - Rajiv Menon: For the POC we'd like to run a Dedicated pool to validate latency at 95th percentile under our concurrency. What does the setup look like?
16:12 - Maya Patel: Typical flow: spin up a Dedicated pool with config matching your GPU/hardware needs, we'll provide an ingress you can route to from your gateway (private VPC or peered). SE will run a benchmark harness — we can use your sample prompts or run our Rex bench. Then we'll produce a report with latency percentiles and token costs.

18:00 - Rajiv Menon: How long to provision a Dedicated pool for POC?
18:05 - Alex Chen: Usually 3-5 business days once we agree on resource sizing and contract for trial credits. For high priority we can shorten provisioning if capacity available.

20:30 - Tom Brooks: A practical question: caching. We already implement prefix caching. Does Redwood's KV cache integrate or is it internal only? Could we share cached prefixes across retries?
20:50 - Maya Patel: We have an internal KV cache optimized for the runtime; for Dedicated there's an option to surface a caching API, or you can keep using your gateway cache. Sharing cache across retries is supported as long as the cache key strategy is consistent. We'll share guidance and examples.

23:00 - Sara Lopez: Pricing — is it token-based on Hosted and some mix of reserved monthly for Dedicated?
23:12 - Alex Chen: Correct. Hosted is token-based with tiered discounts. Dedicated is reserved capacity with an hourly GPU charge and a per-token marginal cost. We can send a pricing sheet with example math for your workload.

25:00 - Rajiv Menon: Any gotchas with LangChain or LlamaIndex connector for retrieval? We use Faiss and Milvus for vector stores.
25:20 - Maya Patel: Both connectors support external vector stores; the LlamaIndex connector includes an adapter that pulls from your store and handles serialization. We often recommend pulling embeddings through Redwood or using our embedding endpoints — but you can bring your own vector store. We'll include a Milvus example.

28:10 - Jordan Li: Also worth noting: if you want to localize inference (Private on-prem), we support an on-prem package but that takes longer and has a different commercial setup. For most customers with strict residency, Private is the path; Dedicated is a fast compromise for isolation and performance.

30:35 - Priya Shah: For audit: do you keep raw prompts in logs? What's masking, retention policy?
30:50 - Alex Chen: Default retention masks sensitive fields; for Dedicated you can customize retention and we offer options to disable logging of raw prompts. We'll include specifics in the compliance pack.

33:00 - Sara Lopez: Practical integration question: our codebase uses LangChain chains and an internal request router; can we swap the provider by changing the instantiation to Redwood's adapter? How invasive is that?
33:20 - Maya Patel: Minimal changes typically: swap the LLM provider class and update a couple of config params. We can prepare a migration diff showing exact code changes.

35:40 - Rajiv Menon: For the POC, our success criteria: 95th percentile latency < 200ms for short prompts, cost per 1k tokens below $X (we'll provide target), and seamless integration with our gateway/auth. If we hit that, we'll scope Dedicated 6-12 month reserved capacity.
35:58 - Alex Chen: That sounds reasonable. We'll align the perf plan to those criteria.

37:10 - Tom Brooks: Any special headers we should be aware of for billing attribution? We tag requests with X-Customer-Org and X-Request-ID today.
37:22 - Jordan Li: We ingest these headers and expose them in usage logs so you can do per-org cost breakdown. Also support custom metadata fields in the Console.

39:00 - Sara Lopez: Are there limits on model choices on Dedicated? We use some open models and a fine-tuned variant.
39:15 - Maya Patel: Dedicated supports a curated set of models; we onboard other open models on request. Fine-tuning artifacts can be pinned to a Dedicated pool; we just need to validate compatibility.

41:30 - Rajiv Menon: Okay good. Let's recap next steps.
41:36 - Alex Chen: Recap: we'll send pricing and contract template; Maya will prepare the Dedicated perf checklist and benchmark plan; we'll share SDK repos and LangChain/LlamaIndex snippets; security will get the SOC2/compliance pack; NimbleGrid to share traffic profile and residency requirements. Schedule the POC kickoff for two weeks.

42:00 - Priya Shah: Thanks. Please include specifics on KMS integration and key rotation in the pack.
42:08 - Alex Chen: Will do.

48:00 - Rajiv Menon: One last question — do you support per-route model selection? We sometimes route some requests to a faster smaller model for low-critical flows.
48:15 - Maya Patel: Yes — routing policies supported in the Control Plane. You can set per-route model pinning and automatic fallback rules for graceful degradation.

50:20 - Alex Chen: Great. Thanks all. We'll follow up with the links and docs.
50:28 - Rajiv Menon: Appreciate it. Looking forward to the POC.
50:35 - Sara Lopez: Thanks everyone.
50:40 - (call ends)
